reconstruction.scope: Imperial Gate (Bab-i Humayun) only, second authored member of18 required Topkapi Palace structures. Broad low brick gatehouse on its particular native rectangular footprint, marble frontispieces/blind pointed niches, tall recessed pointed portals framing a genuinely open lower vaulted route, green-grey paired stone columns/stepped capitals, opaque dark-green upper panels with original geometric gold accents, stone plinth/coping and fine dentils. Inclined occupied paving follows existing front/rear standard-ground controls. No lost upper storey, twin Salutation towers, courtyard canopy, neighbouring fountain, copied calligraphy/tughra/inscription art, furnished guard rooms, visitors or temporary entry/security equipment.

reconstruction.heightBasis: The native parent has no qualified architectural height. Picture-led working wall10.7m/coping11.15m, open lower passage4.15m above its inclined floor with clear width3.8m, tall pointed recesses to about9m plus local grade, marble jambs to about9.7m plus grade. Working frontispiece/niche/panel/column proportions, dentil counts and low inaccessible roof cap remain approximate visualization geometry, not surveyed dimensions or present-condition/engineering/access certification. The current low single-volume profile is modelled; no removed upper storey is reconstructed. Fine wall and ceiling art is excluded.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Original standard PMTiles/Mapzen terrain retained. Existing front path control internal[0,18] supplies nativeY0; rear control[0,-18] supplies only a modest slope for occupied paving and the vaulted passage ceiling. Walls remain vertical and roof/coping level; foundations reach original boundary minima. Ground opening stays tightly inside the occupied parent, while the route through the gate remains open. No precinct slab, neighbouring fountain geometry or terrain flattening. Original native terrain, footprint ownership, facing and open-route fit were visually inspected2026-10-21. Approximate exterior placement is accepted; exact thresholds and host terrain accuracy remain outside scope.
